title: 2005 AMC 10A 17
statement: In the five-sided star shown, the letters \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) and \(E\) are replaced by the numbers \(3,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) and \(9,\) although not necessarily in this order. The sums of the numbers at the ends of the line segments \(AB,\) \(BC,\) \(CD,\) \(DE,\) and \(EA\) form an arithmetic sequence, although not necessarily in this order. What is the middle term of the arithmetic sequence?

solutions.text:
Every number is an endpoint of two segments, so the five segment sums total \(2(3 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 9) = 60.\) The middle term of a five-term arithmetic sequence equals its mean, which is \(\dfrac{60}{5} = 12.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Each of the five numbers is an endpoint of exactly two of the segments
The five segment sums total \(2(3 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 9),\) and the middle term of a five-term arithmetic sequence is its mean
